chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Hussein ibn al-Mukhtar, linking it up through his chain to Salman, may God have Mercy upon him,
that he said in his hadith: 'Whoever takes a female slave and does not have intercourse with her once every forty days, and then she commits a forbidden act, the burden of that sin is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master does not have intercourse with his female slave for forty days?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq cites this narration from Salman al-Farsi to establish the principle of 'kafā’ah' (sufficiency) in the sexual rights of a female slave, emphasizing the owner's duty to prevent her from falling into sin due to neglect. This ruling highlights the reciprocal responsibility in master-slave relations, where the owner’s failure to provide regular intimacy transfers the burden of her subsequent illicit acts to him. It serves as a practical legal mechanism in Shia jurisprudence to ensure the moral and physical well-being of the slave within the household.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-7 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn al-Mukhtar who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Salman - may God have Mercy upon him,
“If one takes a female slave and doesn’t have sex with her once every forty days resulting in her committing a forbidden act, he would be held responsible for her sin.”
